content: Vonoprazan is indicated for the treatment of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection. It should be administered for 14 days, with or without food. The dosing schedule is as follows: Morning dose: 20 mg of vonoprazan (one tablet) and 1,000 mg of amoxicillin (two capsules). Mid-day dose: 1,000 mg of amoxicillin (two yellow capsules). Evening dose: 20 mg of vonoprazan (one tablet) and 1,000 mg of amoxicillin (two capsules). The safety and efficacy of vonoprazan have not been fully established in certain contexts. Specific drug interactions are as follows: 1. Rilpivirine: Vonoprazan decreases the level or effect of rilpivirine by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Amobarbital, apalutamide, armodafinil, belzutifan, bexarotene, bosentan, butabarbital, butalbital, carbamazepine, cenobamate, dabrafenib, efavirenz, elagolix, encorafenib, enzalutamide, eslicarbazepine acetate, etravirine, fosphenytoin, ivosedinib, lorlantinib, lumacaftor/ivacaftor, mitapivat, mitotane, modafinil, nafcillin, pentobarbital, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, rifabutin, rifampin, rifapentine, St. John’s Wort, and sotorasib: These drugs decrease the level or effect of vonoprazan by affecting hepatic or intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Atazanavir, dasatinib, erlotinib, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nelfinavir: Vonoprazan decreases the level or effect of these drugs by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. For itraconazole and ketoconazole, separate administration by at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after vonoprazan. 4. Alfentanil, carbamazepine, cilostazol, citalopram, clonidine, colchicine, cyclosporine, dihydroergotamine, disopyramide, ergotamine, ethosuximide, everolimus, fentanyl, midazolam, pacritinib, pimozide, quinidine, quinine, repaglinide, sirolimus, tacrolimus, theophylline, triazolam: Vonoprazan increases the level or effect of these drugs by affecting hepatic or intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is advised with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 5. Clopidogrel: Vonoprazan decreases the level or effect of clopidogrel by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan may reduce plasma concentrations of the active metabolite of clopidogrel, potentially reducing platelet inhibition. 6. Iron-containing compounds (e.g., ferric carboxymaltose, ferric citrate, ferric derisomaltose, ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferric pyrophosphate, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, ferumoxytol, iron dextran complex, iron sucrose, polysaccharide iron): Vonoprazan decreases the level or effect of these compounds by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Mycophenolate: Vonoprazan decreases the level or effect of mycophenolate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium may be less sensitive to this interaction. 8. Cilostazol: Vonoprazan increases the level or effect of cilostazol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong or moderate inhibitors of CYP2C19. 9. Itraconazole and ketoconazole: Vonoprazan decreases the level or effect of these drugs by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after vonoprazan. In summary, vonoprazan has significant interactions with various drugs, primarily through its effects on CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism or GI absorption. Careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or alternative therapies may be required depending on the co-administered drug.
